title: The Effects of Peracetic Acid on Post‐Larvae and Juvenile Pacific White Shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) and Seven Vibrio Species Isolates at Two Salinities
content:
ABSTRACT

Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) are among the most important aquaculture species but are highly susceptible to Vibrio infections. Novel disease management strategies are necessary. Previous studies have reported that peracetic acid (PAA) is an effective disinfectant, but its application in shrimp aquaculture remains underexplored. This study aimed to determine the median lethal concentration (LC50) of PAA at two life stages of L. vannamei under two salinities and assess its in vitro growth-inhibitory effects against Vibrio spp. Two groups of 180 juveniles (~5 g) and post-larvae (maintained at either 4 or 30 g L−1) were exposed to six geometrically increasing concentrations of PAA to determine 24-h LC50 estimates. Representative juvenile shrimp tissues were histologically assessed. Seven isolates of Vibrio spp. inocula were exposed to PAA and enumerated to determine growth inhibition. The LC50 estimates varied from 29.09 to 82.40 mg L−1 of PAA. Gill and hepatopancreas tissues were notably damaged at 40.5 and 75 mg L−1 of PAA at 4 and 30 g L−1, respectively. Growth of all Vibrio spp. was inhibited at the lowest PAA dose tested, that being 0.03125 mg L−1 after 45 min. These findings will help progress the further application of peracetic acid in shrimp aquaculture.
